hints: Focus on atom balance, since atoms are never lost, the carbon from $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$ must all end up in the hydrocarbon.
Start with aluminium and sodium, you need 4 $\text{NaAlO}_2$ to balance the 4 Al, which fixes the number of $\text{NaOH}$ at 4.
Now balance oxygen with water and then count hydrogens, all 12 H atoms on the left must appear in the hydrocarbon molecules containing 3 carbons in total.
walkthrough:
**Write the skeleton equation**

Think of this as a puzzle where every atom must be accounted for. Let us write what we know.

$$\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 + \text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{NaAlO}_2 + \text{hydrocarbon}$$

**Balance Al and Na first**

These are the easiest because they only appear in one place on each side. We have 4 Al on the left, so we need 4 $\text{NaAlO}_2$ on the right.

$$\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 + 4\text{NaOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{NaAlO}_2 + \text{hydrocarbon}$$
That also balances Na, 4 on each side. Well done.

**Balance O using water**

Now look at oxygen. On the right we have $4 \times 2 = 8$ O atoms in $4\text{NaAlO}_2$. On the left we already have 4 O from $4\text{NaOH}$, so we need 4 more O from water.

$$\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 + 4\text{NaOH} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{NaAlO}_2 + \text{hydrocarbon}$$

**Count H and C to find the hydrocarbon**

Count H on the left: $4$ from NaOH plus $8$ from water gives $12$ H in total. All of this must go into the hydrocarbon.
Count C on the left: $3$ C atoms must also go into the hydrocarbon. The only way to fit 3 C and 12 H is as $3$ molecules of $\text{CH}_4$. So the hydrocarbon is methane, $\text{CH}_4$.

options.A: Correct. 3 molecules of $\text{CH}_4$ give 3 C and 12 H, exactly matching the 3 C from $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$ and the 12 H from $4\text{NaOH} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The fully balanced equation is $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3 + 4\text{NaOH} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 4\text{NaAlO}_2 + 3\text{CH}_4$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ has the wrong C:H ratio for this balance. To get 3 carbons you would need 1.5 molecules, which is impossible, and the H count would not give 12 H.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8$ has the right number of carbons (3) but the wrong number of hydrogens. It only provides 8 H, while the reactants supply 12 H that must go into the hydrocarbon. This is a common trap if you forget to balance oxygen with water first.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$ has far too many carbons. We only start with 3 C atoms from $\text{Al}_4\text{C}_3$, so we can never make a $\text{C}_6$ product without creating carbon atoms.
